analysis:
This batch has only documentation and changelog changes: two new changelog.d fragments and a docs/developer/build.md addition at head lines 38-42. No executable source was supplied.

The fresh-mdm-removal-guidance fragment says `darkbloom status` and both `darkbloom doctor` authorization summaries will stop offering MDM removal when the coordinator decision is too old for removal readiness. The provider-status-app-attest-lease fragment says status/doctor will report App Attest authorization until the coordinator lease expires, instead of requiring a renewal within the last 10 seconds. Both state that `darkbloom unenroll` keeps its stricter 10-second renewal check before offering MDM removal.

These statements are consistent with TB-011, T-052 and T-057. TB-011 requires a fresh current coordinator decision before removal guidance, keeps serving separate from MDM removal, and treats badges and diagnostics as non-authoritative. The status/doctor display change affects reporting only. Serving authorization stays with the coordinator through authorizeInferenceHandoff and the final-writer checks.

The actual code for status/doctor is not in the supplied evidence, so I could not confirm that the freshness gating matches the changelog. Likewise, I could not check that the "unexpired lease stays visible" display does not suggest local trust. The prior-art wording keeps MDM removal tied to receipt-monitoring readiness, which suggests the display is only conservative.

The build.md addition tells developers to rebuild the provider test product before running the authorization guidance tests. It says those tests exercise shared production decisions without native Apple operations, and that signed-release qualification stays separate. This makes no new qualification claim and adds no new attack surface.

I found no security regression. The Swift source behind the status, doctor and unenroll summaries should be reviewed in whatever batch contains it, to confirm the fresh-decision gating for MDM removal.
